title: Fibre Server — Operator
description: Single-operator view of one or more Celestia Fibre servers (celestia-app v10.4.0 metric surface). The fibre server pushes OTLP metrics (--otel-endpoint) to an OpenTelemetry Collector, which exposes them on :8889 for Prometheus to scrape; this dashboard queries that Prometheus. Pick your Prometheus datasource and server instance(s) above.

panels.title: Servers reporting
panels.description: Servers represented by the periodically exported occupancy gauge, including idle servers. The collector expires cached metrics after 2 minutes without new data; scrape availability alone does not prove Fibre is healthy.

panels.title: UploadShard rate
panels.description: Completed UploadShard RPCs per second across the selected servers.

panels.title: DownloadShard rate
panels.description: Completed DownloadShard RPCs per second across the selected servers.

panels.title: Budget utilization
panels.description: Limiter occupancy divided by enforced positive storage budgets across selected servers. Servers with a non-positive, unenforced budget are excluded. This is not physical disk utilization.

panels.title: Uploads rejected
panels.description: UploadShard RPCs rejected by the storage limiter over the selected time range. At celestia-app v10.4.0 the only rejection reason is budget_exceeded.

panels.title: Sign p50
panels.description: Median time for a Fibre payment-promise signing attempt, including the signer RPC and any backend waiting. Interpret alongside activity and signing failures; this is separate from consensus KMS signing latency.

panels.title: Last upload success age
panels.description: Time since the last successful upload (worst across selected servers). Empty before the first success. Increasing age is normal while idle; it is not an outage or missed-endorsement verdict.

panels.title: Uploads (UploadShard RPCs served by your server)
UploadShard duration heatmap
panels.description: Distribution of UploadShard RPC latency. Explicit buckets (s): 0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2.5, 5.

panels.title: UploadShard rate & in-flight
panels.description: Completed UploadShard RPCs per second and currently executing UploadShard RPCs.

panels.title: Upload throughput
panels.description: Successful upload shard-row payload bytes per second, including repeated successful uploads. Includes encoded/padded row data; excludes protocol overhead and failed transfers. This is not unique disk growth or NIC bandwidth.

panels.title: Rejected uploads by reason
panels.description: UploadShard rejections per second, split by reason. At celestia-app v10.4.0 the only emitted reason is budget_exceeded (storage budget full); rejected clients get a RetryInfo hint of one prune interval.

panels.title: Downloads (DownloadShard RPCs served by your server)
DownloadShard duration heatmap
panels.description: Distribution of DownloadShard RPC latency (same buckets as uploads).

panels.title: DownloadShard rate & in-flight
panels.description: Completed DownloadShard RPCs per second and currently executing DownloadShard RPCs.

panels.title: Download throughput
panels.description: Shard-row payload bytes read for successful download handlers per second, before returning the response. Excludes protocol overhead; does not prove full client receipt or measure NIC bandwidth.

panels.title: DownloadShard success rate
panels.description: Share of DownloadShard RPCs completing successfully.

panels.title: Occupancy vs budget
panels.description: Occupancy = shard bytes tracked by the storage limiter (on-disk plus in-flight reserved; not a disk gauge). Budget = per-node storage budget derived by the server (stake-proportional, scaled by the liveness inverse and clamped). Over-budget uploads are rejected.

panels.title: Budget utilization
panels.description: Limiter occupancy divided by enforced positive storage budget. Servers with a non-positive, unenforced budget are omitted; this is not filesystem usage.

panels.title: Store put/get p95
panels.description: Shard storage engine latency. Buckets (s): 0.001 … 1.

panels.title: Backend get by outcome
panels.description: Shard-backend reads per second for the primary backend, split by outcome (success, not_found, timeout, canceled, throttled, error).

panels.title: Backend get bytes rate
panels.description: Encoded shard bytes read per second from the primary backend (local or object storage).

panels.title: Sign duration percentiles
panels.description: Time for Fibre payment-promise signing attempts, including the signer RPC and any backend waiting. Compare against your normal baseline and failure rate; no universal 10 ms threshold applies to this instrument.

panels.title: Sign rate & failures
panels.description: Payment-promise signing attempts per second, including failures, and failed signing attempts per second.

panels.title: Prune entries rate
panels.description: Shards deleted per second. The counter only increases when a prune cycle actually deletes shards — a flat zero while occupied is expected until shards pass their prune deadline (max(ExpiresAt, creation + shard_retention, default 4h)).

panels.title: Prune duration p95 & failures
panels.description: Prune cycle latency and failed prune cycles.

panels.title: Prune loop runs
panels.description: Completed prune cycles per second. The loop normally runs once per minute (~0.017 runs/s). Zero means no completed cycles observed; check telemetry, cycle duration and server logs for a stuck cycle or stopped loop.

panels.title: In-flight RPCs
panels.description: Concurrent upload, download and backend-read RPCs. These counts are not QUIC connection utilization. Correlate rising concurrency with request latency and errors; connection saturation needs configured limits and additional instrumentation.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: Live goroutines in the fibre server process.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: Runtime-managed memory excluding released heap pages, split into stacks and other Go memory. Other includes more than the heap. This is not process RSS or host memory.

panels.title: Memory limit vs GC goal
panels.description: Configured Go memory limit and garbage-collector heap target. The limit series may be absent when GOMEMLIMIT is unlimited. These are not physical host memory capacity.

panels.title: Traffic over the selected time range
Upload payload volume
panels.description: Increase in successful upload shard-row payload bytes over the selected range. Includes successful duplicates and coding/padding. This is not unique blob volume or NIC traffic.

panels.title: Download payload volume
panels.description: Increase in payload bytes read by successful download handlers over the selected range. Does not include protocol overhead or prove complete client receipt.

panels.title: Completed upload RPCs
panels.description: Completed upload RPCs over the selected range, including failed attempts. A request is not a unique blob or a settlement.

panels.title: Completed download RPCs
panels.description: Completed download RPCs over the selected range, including failed attempts. Idle or new servers may have no samples. Increases are estimated between scrape samples.
